# ADR 0034 §2.3: the credential window is a native password field

## Context

- **The operator's ask.** On 2026-09-26 @tobiu asked why the packaged shell asks for a PAT in a window that is only text: *"why not use a PasswordField? I would not know that cmd+v would work."* That window is the shell's one credential surface. It serves plane attach and every credential-bearing Fleet verb (`connectTenant`, `defineAgent`).
- **The Institution change.** neomjs/neo-agent-institution#227 replaces the window with a native `<input type="password">` inside the same isolated, script-free window.
- **Why the ADR moves first.** That puts credential bytes in a renderer. ADR 0034 §2.3 forbids this today, and its own falsifier requires an amendment first: *"any leaf needing a renderer capability … amends THIS section first … it never … moves secret bytes into renderer state as a leaf-local decision."*

## The Problem

The text that binds today (`learn/agentos/decisions/0034-electron-shell-architecture.md`, dev@6b37906b9a):
- **Anti-anchor row:** *"credential or token bytes in renderer-readable state (§2.3)"*.
- **§2.3 heading:** *"credentials never renderer-readable"*.
- **§2.3 item 8 (`attachPlane`):** *"collects the PAT in the main-custody credential window (the page receives no key or paste data)"*.

The window that item 8 describes shows no field and no button. Its only verbs are Enter and Escape, and it reports its length in the title bar.

It is also **less** secure than a native field. On macOS, Chromium turns on Secure Event Input only while a native password field has focus. A page with no input element never gets it, so today a typed PAT is readable by any process holding Input Monitoring.

## The Architectural Reality

| | Element-less window (today) | Native password field (#227) |
|---|---|---|
| Secure Event Input (macOS) | off: typed keys readable via Input Monitoring | **on while focused, off after settle**, measured below |
| Caret, selection, undo, ⌘V, AX secure-text role | none: editing emulated in main | the platform's own |
| Where the bytes live while typing | main | the credential window's renderer, until submit |
| Cockpit renderer / App Worker | never | never (unchanged) |

Measured on Electron 43.1.0 (darwin), driving #227's module:
- `ioreg -l -w 0` showed `kCGSSessionSecureInputPID` = the probe's own main PID while the field had focus, and no holder after the prompt settled.
- Submit resolved the exact typed value. Cancel, Escape, closing the window and a whitespace-only Enter each behaved as specified.
- The page ran zero scripts.

## The Fix

Amend §2.3. No other section changes.

1. **New item 9, "The credential window."**
   - The window collects the credential in a native password field, in a sandboxed, context-isolated window of its own.
   - Its document carries no script, under CSP `default-src 'none'`.
   - A window-only preload hands the value to main once, on submit, over that window's own `webContents.ipc`.
   - Main destroys the window on every settle path: submit, cancel, close, renderer gone.
   - Main alone holds the credential after submit. The cockpit's renderer and the App Worker never hold it (items 5–6 unchanged).
   - Rationale: platform Secure Event Input and native editing, measured.
2. **Item 8** drops *"(the page receives no key or paste data)"* and points to item 9.
3. **The anti-anchor row and §2.3's heading** scope the ban to renderer-readable state *outside the credential window (§2.3.9)*.
4. **Provenance** follows items 7 and 8: *(amended 2026-09-26, #N — for neomjs/neo-agent-institution#227)*.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §2.3 carries item 9 as specified. Item 8's parenthetical, the anti-anchor row and §2.3's heading are scoped to it, with the provenance bracket.
- [ ] No other ADR text changes. Items 5–6 (the per-boot token and seat PATs) stay exactly as they are.

## Out of Scope

- The Institution implementation: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#227.
- The cockpit's dev-server-topology PasswordFields (item 6's transitional path).

## Decision Record impact

amends ADR 0034 §2.3 (items 8–9, the anti-anchor row, the heading).
